newsitem.title: FRANCE: Riviera mayor re-imposes begging ban.
newsitem.headline: Riviera mayor re-imposes begging ban.

text.p: The conservative mayor of Nice, "capital" of the French Riviera, reinstated on Tuesday a controversial local by-law banning begging in the city during the summer holiday season.

Mayor Jacques Peyrat of the Rally for the Republic Gaullist party ordered the law reinstated after a local court turned down, with minor changes, an appeal by the local prosecutor to have the by-law declared illegal.
The prosecutor argued that in France's current difficult economic situation the by-law disturbed public order and created more problems than it solved.
But the court, while striking out four articles as "imprecise", said the by-law was legal, opening the way for Peyrat to order its re-imposition.
Nice, with its balmy weather, is a top holiday destination and a prime retirement town and Peyrat imposed the ban on the grounds that aggressive begging disturbed tourists and pensioners.
Under the ban, first introduced last summer, municipal police can forcibly remove beggars from town and take them to an isolated hostel several miles (km) away for food and shelter.
Those who refused to stay could leave once they arrived but they argued that they then had to walk back because the hostel was away from any public transport.
Several other French holiday towns imposed similar bans last year, raising the ire of civil rights groups.
Peyrat organised a referendum on the issue in Nice in November in which 66 percent of those who voted agreed with the ban. But 77 percent of eligible voters abstained.
